items.title: 7.6 Air columns (hawa ke columns) mein stationary waves (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 7.6 with Figs. 7.8 and 7.9 and Examples 7.4 and 7.5 (PDF 150-155).

blocks.text: Stationary waves doosre media mein bhi ban sakti hain, jaise kisi pipe ya tube ke andar hawa ka column. Vibrate karte hawa ke column ki aam misal organ pipe hai.
Organ pipe

Organ pipe wind instrument (hawa se bajne wala saaz) hai jis mein hawa ke column mein stationary waves banne se sound (awaz) paida hoti hai. Yeh ek lambi hollow (khokhli) tube hai jis ke dono sire khule hote hain, ya ek sira khula aur doosra band. Aane wali (incident) aur palatne wali (reflected) wave ka relation (taalluq) is par depend karta hai ke pipe ka reflect karne wala sira khula hai ya band.

items: (i) Agar reflect karne wala sira khula ho to hawa ke molecules poori freedom (azaadi) se hil sakte hain, aur yeh sira antinode ban jata hai.
(ii) Agar reflect karne wala sira band ho to yeh node ban jata hai, kyunke wahan molecules ki motion (harkat) ruki hui hai.

blocks.text: Vibration ke modes
Pipe mein stationary longitudinal waves neeche ki do cases mein samjhi jati hain:
Case (1): Dono siron se khule organ pipe mein vibration ke modes

Length (lambai) l ka organ pipe lein jo dono siron se khula hai. Khule sire par hawa ka molecule poori azaadi se hil sakta hai, is liye wahan antinode banta hai, jaisa Fig. 7.8 mein hai. Is figure mein pipe ke andar ki longitudinal waves ko transverse (lehar jaisi) lines se dikhaya gaya hai; yeh lines pipe ke axis ke saath different (alag alag) points par hawa ke particles ka displacement aur amplitude batati hain.

blocks.alt: Dono siron se khule teen pipes, rang bhare displacement ke ghere ke sath. (a) beech mein ek node, l = lambda1/2, f1 = v/2l; (b) do nodes, l = 2(lambda2/2), f2 = 2(v/2l); (c) teen nodes, l = 3(lambda3/2), f3 = 3(v/2l). (a) aur (b) ke oopar hare do-teer antinodes aur nuqte nodes dikhate hain.

Case (2): Ek sire se band organ pipe mein vibration ke modes
Length l ka organ pipe lein jo ek sire se band hai. Band sire par node aur khule sire par antinode banta hai, jaisa Fig. 7.9 mein hai.

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Band sire par hawa hil nahi sakti, is liye wahan hamesha node hai, aur khule sire par antinode. Is liye pipe ki length chauthai wavelength ka sirf odd (taaq) multiple ho sakti hai: l = λ/4, 3λ/4, 5λ/4, aur frequencies f₁, 3f₁, 5f₁.
(b) Vibration ka doosra (second) mode
Doosre mode mein do nodes aur do antinodes hote hain (Fig. 7.9 b).

Ise third harmonic kehte hain (yeh vibration ka doosra mode hai).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab f₃ = 3f₁ ko “second harmonic” kehti hai. Harmonic ka number frequency ko f₁ se divide kar ke milta hai: f₁ first, 2f₁ second aur 3f₁ third harmonic hai, jaisa kitab khud khule pipe aur string ke liye batati hai. Ek sire se band pipe mein 2f₁ hota hi nahi, is liye 3f₁ third harmonic hai; haan, yeh vibration ka doosra (second) mode zaroor hai.

blocks.title: A Scientific Fact (ek scientific haqeeqat)
blocks.text: Organ pipe mein sound chalane ka main driving mechanism (asal zariya) flue-slit (patli jhiri) se nikalne wali hawa ki wavering (kaanpti hui), chadar jaisi jet (dhaar) hai. Yeh jet pipe ke oopar wale hont (upper lip) aur pipe ke hawa ke column se mil kar constant (mustaqil) oscillation qaim rakhti hai.

Dono cases ko parh kar result (nateeja) yeh hai ke dono siron se khula pipe ek sire se band pipe ke muqable mein harmonics mein richer (zyada harmonics wala) hai: khule pipe mein saare harmonics, band pipe mein sirf odd harmonics.

blocks.title: Example 7.4
blocks.problem: Ek organ pipe ki length 50 cm hai. Us ke fundamental note aur agle harmonic ki frequency nikalein jab pipe (a) dono siron se khula ho, (b) ek sire se band ho. (Sound ki speed = 350 m s⁻¹)
steps: Diya gaya: l = 50 cm = 50/100 m = 0.5 m, v = 350 m s⁻¹.
(a) Dono siron se khula pipe: f₁ = ?, f₂ = ?. Khule pipe mein nth harmonic: fₙ = n (v/2l), n = 1, 2, 3, ….
(b) Ek sire se band pipe: f₁ = ?, f₃ = ?. Band pipe mein fₙ = n (v/4l), n = 1, 3, 5, 7, … (sirf odd).
Agla harmonic n = 3 hai (2 maujood nahi): f₃ = 3v/4l = (3 × 350)/(4 × 0.5).
blocks.answer: Khula pipe: 350 Hz aur 700 Hz. Band pipe: 175 Hz aur f₃ = 525 Hz.

blocks.title: Ponder Upon (ghaur karein)
blocks.text: Khule pipes saare harmonics paida karte hain, jabke band pipes sirf odd (taaq) harmonics.

blocks.title: Example 7.5
blocks.problem: Church ka organ different length ke pipes se bana hai, har pipe ek sire se khula (doosra band) hai. Sab se chhota pipe 30 mm aur sab se lamba 4 m hai. Fundamental notes ki frequency range nikalein. (Sound ki speed = 340 m s⁻¹)
steps: Diya gaya: l_min = 30 mm = 30/1000 m = 30 × 10⁻³ m, l_max = 4 m, v = 340 m s⁻¹; frequency range = ?
Ek sire se khule (doosre se band) pipe ke liye: fₙ = nv/4l.
(i) Sab se chhota pipe, n = 1: f₁,max = nv/4l_min = (1 × 340)/(4 × 30 × 10⁻³) = 2833.33 Hz. Chhota pipe, oonchi frequency.
(ii) Sab se lamba pipe, n = 1: f₁,min = nv/4l_max = (1 × 340)/(4 × 4) = 21.25 Hz. Lamba pipe, neechi frequency.
blocks.answer: Fundamental frequency ki range taqreeban 21 Hz se 2833 Hz tak hai.

blocks.title: Brain Teaser
blocks.text: Flute bajane wala dekhta hai ke flute thori si sharp (zarurat se oonchi) pitch de rahi hai. Is ki kya wajah ho sakti hai? (Jawab neeche self-check mein.)

blocks.caption: Khule aur band pipes (khulasa)
rows: band sire par node, khule par antinode

blocks.prompt: Ek organ pipe 1 m lamba hai; jab yeh dono siron se khula ho aur jab ek sire se band ho, to fundamental aur agle do harmonics nikalein, v = 340 m s⁻¹ (numerical 7.9). Flute bajane wala dekhta hai ke flute thori sharp (oonchi) baj rahi hai; is ki kya wajah ho sakti hai (Brain Teaser)?
blocks.explanation: Khula pipe: f₁ = v/2l = 340/2 = 170 Hz, phir 2f₁ = 340 Hz aur 3f₁ = 510 Hz. Band pipe: f₁ = v/4l = 340/4 = 85 Hz, phir sirf odd harmonics 3f₁ = 255 Hz aur 5f₁ = 425 Hz. Flute: bajane se andar ki hawa garam ho jati hai aur garam hawa mein sound ki speed v barh jati hai; har frequency v ke proportional hai, is liye poori flute sharp bajti hai. Head joint ko zyada andar dhakelna (hawa ka column chhota karna) bhi pitch oonchi karta hai.

blocks.text: Summary (khulasa)

items: Organ pipe: khula sira antinode, band sira node.
Dono taraf khula: λ₁ = 2l, f₁ = v/2l; fₙ = nf₁, λₙ = 2l/n (saare harmonics).
Ek taraf band: λ₁ = 4l, f₁ = v/4l; λ₃ = 4l/3, f₃ = 3f₁ (third harmonic); λₙ = 4l/n, n odd (sirf odd harmonics).
Example 7.4: 350/700 Hz (khula), 175/525 Hz (band). Example 7.5: 21 Hz se 2833 Hz.
